articles.title: Sunderland University relocated gallery set for first exhibition
articles.summary: The Northern Gallery for Contemporary Art opens in September after the closure of the Glass Centre.
articles.body:
The first exhibition of an art gallery forced to move to new premises has been announced.

The Northern Gallery for Contemporary Art (NGCA) is moving to the Culture House in Sunderland on 12 September, opening with an exhibition on local artist Audrey Amiss.

The University of Sunderland, which runs the gallery, said Kitchen Sink Realism would feature previously unseen paintings and drawings, as well as archival material by the late Sunderland-born artist.

The gallery was previously housed at the National Glass Centre, which shut in July after the university said it could not afford building repairs.

Despite being a prolific artist, it was only after her death in 2013 that Amiss' breadth of work came to light.

She is known for her campaigning against harmful treatment in the mental health system, after a crisis she suffered as a student in the 1950s.

Her exhibition will be on display until 17 January, and the university is offering printmaking workshops on the opening weekend.

Kevin Petrie, professor of creative practice at the university, said the gallery was a "long-standing asset" for students.

"It gives them the chance to work alongside the exhibition curator, and in many cases artists themselves, to learn first-hand about careers and professional practice in the arts," he said.

Culture House will also house a library, podcasting studios and a sky garden when it opens.

articles.title: Dozens of new wildfires break out across Greece
articles.summary: Thirty-nine new wildfires have broken out across Greece within the space of a few hours, the fire service reported on Tuesday. The most severe fire is raging...
articles.body:
Thirty-nine new wildfires have broken out across Greece within the space of a few hours, the fire service reported on Tuesday.

The most severe fire is raging on the island of Salamis, off the coast of Athens, according to firefighters.

The island is home to the Greek Navy's largest base. According to firefighters on the ground, the base was not at risk.

The fire raged through a gorge and was tackled by numerous firefighting aircraft and helicopters. In addition, large fire brigade units and volunteers have been deployed, broadcaster ERT reported.

Due to the ongoing drought, the risk of wildfires remains high across large parts of Greece, according to the civil defence agency.

Temperatures in central Athens reached 40 degrees Celsius on Tuesday and the current heatwave has been forecast to persist until the beginning of next week.

articles.title: Lake America? Trump's latest salvo against Canada takes ties to uncharted waters
articles.summary: US News: TOI Correspondent From Washington: US-Canada relations are in danger of tipping into Niagara Falls, which straddles both countries, after MAGA boss Do.
articles.body: TOI Correspondent From Washington: US-Canada relations are in danger of tipping into Niagara Falls, which straddles both countries, after MAGA boss Donald Trump threatened to rename Lake Ontario, into which the storied waterfall empties -- as Lake America. Ontarioâs pugnacious premier Doug Ford in turn effectively said "bring it on," warning of cutting electricity exports to the US and restricting critical minerals such as nickel and uranium.The latest installment of the increasingly surreal trade war between neighbors who have the longest peaceful and unmilitarized border in the world (8891 kms) came after Trump decided that if Canada will not fall in line economically, he will mess with it cartographically.âThe United States is giving serious consideration to changing the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America in that we donât expect to be doing much business with Ontario any longer,â Trump posted on his social media account, with a separate post showing the change in nomenclature.Having already rechristened the Gulf of Mexico the âGulf of America,â the US President appears to be discovering that the North American atlas is offering more opportunities for rebranding, with Venezuela and Cuba possibly next in line. But jokes aside, there is a distinctly serious undertone to the developments where U.S ties with two benign neighbors is turning toxic.Canada on Tuesday announced retaliatory tariffs covering more than 700 American products worth roughly $20 billion after Trump wielded his tariff bazooka first. The measures, due to take effect Sept. 8, include tariffs of 15%, 25% and 50% on American exports ranging from steel and dairy to appliances, seafood and cosmetics. Ottawa also announced a C$7.5 billion support package for industries hit by the dispute.The latest confrontation follows the collapse of trade talks after Canadian PM Mark Carney rejected U.S. demands he claimed went beyond trade, touching Canadian cultural and French-language protections. Trump, for his part, insists Canada has been âripping offâ America for decades and says the country is âeasily the most difficult and unreasonableâ trading partner, even as he denied having problems with Canadaâs French heritage.âI would never interfere with Canadians speaking French! In fact, I have never even thought of doing such a stupid thing. This lie was made up by a weak and ineffective Prime Minister in an attempt to gain political support, which he has totally lost, from the people of Quebec. I love French Canadians!â Trump wrote.There is a delicious historical irony to Trump's proposed renaming campaign. âOntarioâ is derived from the Iroquoian word kanadario, generally translated as âsparkling water.â âCanadaâ itself is said to come from the Huron-Iroquois word kanata, meaning âvillageâ or âsettlement.â And âAmericaâ? That name wasn't exactly minted in Philadelphia. It came from Amerigo Vespucci, the Italian explorer, with German cartographer Martin WaldseemÃ¼ller first putting âAmericaâ on his 1507 map.So, historically speaking, the names of both countries and the lake in question are products of Indigenous languages and European cartography. Nobody involved in today's quarrel can quite claim to have invented the labels, and the geopolitical equivalent of âfinders, keepersâ is therefore on rather shaky historical ground.The larger casualty from the spat may be something less easily renamed: the extraordinary ease with which the US and Canada once conducted business. For generations, the two countries were the diplomatic equivalent of the neighbors who borrowed each other's lawnmowers and never bothered with keeping the score. Their economies became so intertwined that auto parts can cross the border repeatedly before a finished vehicle emerges; energy, minerals, agriculture and manufacturing operate through deeply integrated supply chains.Trump's aggressive trade strategy has shaken that comfortable arrangement. Carney has said Canada will return to negotiations if Washington changes its approach, but the relationship has already entered unfamiliar territory. America and Canada used to have the world's longest undefended border. Now the only thing crossing it freely may be heated words.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Autistic DJ befriended at Boomtown Fair offered 'dream' set
articles.summary: Adam, 23, has been asked to play a DJ set at the music event next year after his story went viral.
articles.body:
An autistic man whose story about being befriended by strangers when he attended his first-ever festival alone went viral has been invited to play a DJ set next year.

Adam James, 23, from High Wycombe in Buckinghamshire, "realised his dream" after he made friends with a group of festival-goers who invited him to camp with them at Boomtown Fair in Hampshire.

The lifelong music fan and aspiring drum and bass DJ has now been offered a set at the festival in 2027.

Adam's dad, Andy, whose social media post thanking the "lads from Bristol" who took Adam under their wing has been seen by millions, said he had seen his "son's dreams come true".

"It's made me really, really proud... Adam's over the moon," he added.

The festival's co-founder, Luke Mitchell, commented on a BBC video to say the story had "circled around the Boomtown office with absolute joy".

"Stories like this are why festivals are so incredibly important," he said, before asking Andy: "Can we fix up a DJ set for Adam next year?"

A spokesperson for Boomtown Fair confirmed that they had asked Adam to play a set, with the stage and timings to be announced once programming for next year's event has begun.

Adam, also known as Adzo to his friends, previously said he had been nervous for his first festival experience, but everything had changed after meeting the group when they asked him if he had a mallet to help build their tents.

"I wasn't very confident in myself, but as soon as I was with them, I was fine," he said. "They could have just ignored me, but the fact they saw I was on my own and took me in was just amazing."

Following the viral post, which has been shared and liked by thousands of people, Adam was reunited with the group at the Trident Pub in Bristol and was booked for several gigs.

Since his story has been shared online, Adam has been inundated with offers from DJs and clubs to come to their events and play at their venues, and has even been invited by the Pete Tong Academy to join a DJing course.

Andy told the BBC the reaction had been "absolutely amazing" to see, particularly after Adam had faced cruel comments online in the past.

"He's become very resilient, but he's such a lovely bloke," his dad said. "It means so much to me and his Mum too."

articles.title: Banker allegedly told his longtime friend about a secret $8.1 billion takeover; friend bought $53 million of stock and made $18.5 million
articles.summary: US News: A former senior Bank of America investment banker has been accused by the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) of tipping a longtime friend abo.
articles.body: A former senior Bank of America investment banker has been accused by the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) of tipping a longtime friend about a confidential $8.1 billion takeover, allegedly allowing the friend to make $18.5 million in illegal profits through stock trades.According to Reuters, the SEC on Friday charged Jason Satsky, 59, who previously served as Bank of Americaâs co-head of Americas power and renewable energy banking, with insider trading. The regulator alleges that Satsky shared confidential information with Gavin Wolfe, a longtime friend and former colleague, about a potential acquisition of South Jersey Industries.Friend allegedly bought $53 million worth of sharesThe SEC alleges that Wolfe, who runs Evergreen Capital, purchased more than 2.2 million shares of South Jersey Industries, the parent company of South Jersey Gas, after receiving the alleged tip from Satsky.The shares were worth approximately $53 million. Wolfe reportedly made a 36% gain when South Jersey Industries announced an $8.1 billion buyout on February 24, 2022, generating an alleged profit of about $18.5 million.The SEC's allegations centre on communications between Satsky and Wolfe in the months leading up to the acquisition announcement.Bankers allegedly discussed takeover at basketball gameAccording to the SEC's complaint, Satsky and Wolfe communicated several times about a potential acquisition. Among the encounters cited was a nationally televised college basketball game between Duke and Kentucky at Madison Square Garden in New York.Satsky and Wolfe attended the game with their wives, with Satsky using luxury-box seats obtained through Bank of America.The SEC is seeking to recover the alleged illicit gains from Wolfe and impose civil penalties and officer-and-director bans against both men, among other remedies.Both men deny insider trading allegationsSatsky has strongly denied the SEC's accusations through his lawyer, Robert Anello."Jason strongly denies the SECâs allegations and is confident that the evidence will demonstrate that he acted properly and that he will be fully vindicated," Anello said. He also maintained that Satsky did not provide Wolfe or anyone else with material nonpublic information regarding South Jersey Industries.Wolfe's lawyer, Reed Brodsky, said his client "categorically denies the allegations" and intends to vigorously defend himself. According to Brodsky, the SEC overlooked sworn testimony and documents indicating that Wolfe purchased South Jersey shares based on an "independent investment thesis."Satsky was terminated by Bank of AmericaWolfe, 55, previously worked as a senior power and renewable energy banker at Credit Suisse before joining Bank of America with Satsky in 2012. He now runs Evergreen Capital, which manages assets belonging to his family.The SEC said Bank of America terminated Satsky in March 2025. The bank was not accused of wrongdoing and confirmed that Satsky no longer works for the company.Evergreen did not immediately respond to a request for comment.The case remains an allegation at this stage, and both Satsky and Wolfe have denied wrongdoing.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Israeli military sent US universities millions for weapons research: Report
articles.summary: Middle East News: The Israeli Ministry of Defense and Israeli defence companies have channelled millions of dollars into weapons-related research at US universities, mu.
articles.body: The Israeli Ministry of Defense and Israeli defence companies have channelled millions of dollars into weapons-related research at US universities, much of it through funding arrangements that were not consistently disclosed in federal databases, according to an investigation by Drop Site News.The investigation found financial links between Israelâs Ministry of Defense, weapons manufacturers and dozens of American universities over the past two decades. These included research grants, tuition payments and other forms of institutional funding, with records dating from 2004 to 2025.According to Drop Site News, an analysis of university and state audit records identified more than $15 million in funding linked to the Israeli Ministry of Defense or Israeli defence companies that was either unreported or reported inconsistently. The publication said the actual figure could be higher because some university records did not disclose funding amounts, while others contained conflicting information.The investigation identified ties involving prominent institutions including Columbia, Cornell, Princeton, Harvard, Northwestern, Georgia Tech, the University of Connecticut, the University of Maryland and the University of California, Berkeley.Among the Israeli companies involved were defence giants Elbit Systems, Rafael and Israel Aerospace Industries, with records showing sponsorship of research projects related to military technologies.At the University of Connecticut, for example, federal audit records show an Israeli Ministry of Defense-funded project titled âImpact Point Prediction Research for Short & Medium Range Thrusting Projectilesâ. The project received $668,456 across nine fiscal years between 2013 and 2023. Another project, âHigh Sensitivity SQUIDs for Magnetic Field Detectionâ, received $251,336 over the same period.US law requires universities receiving federal assistance to report foreign gifts and contracts worth at least $250,000 in a calendar year. However, Drop Site found that some Israeli funding did not consistently appear in the federal disclosure system.The findings come amid renewed tensions between Israel and the US over Israeli military actions in the region. articles.title: United's biggest-ever international expansion includes 10 destinations worth a closer look
articles.summary: The Chicago-based carrier will offer new nonstop flights across Europe and Asia, making places like Marseille, Valencia and Okinawa easier to reach.
articles.body:
Ever wanted to fly nonstop to Slovenia? You're in Luxembourg!

United Airlines on Tuesday announced what the airline says is the largest expansion in its history, with 10 new international destinations — including the first nonstop flights by a U.S. airline to Ljubljana, Slovenia and Luxembourg City — and 13 new routes.

"We've opened up more of the world to our customers," Patrick Quayle, United's senior vice president of global network planning, said on a conference call with reporters . "Next summer, we'll give them more opportunities … to explore places that they may not have previously considered."

Beginning in March 2027 and continuing into the summer, United will launch nonstop service to the following destinations across Europe and Asia:

Luxembourg City, Luxembourg — from Newark

Terceira, Azores, Portugal — from Newark

Toulouse, France — from Washington Dulles

The flights to Ibiza, Valencia, Luxembourg City, Marseille and Toulouse will be aboard United's new Airbus A321XLR. The plane is scheduled to begin flying select domestic routes in September, followed by international service in December.

The Chicago-based carrier has added nearly 60 international destinations to its route map since 2017, and now flies to more than 160 international destinations.

United is also adding new international routes to destinations it already serves from three of its U.S. hubs: daily service from Los Angeles to Osaka, Japan; nonstop service from Washington, D.C., to Milan, Italy; and daily nonstop service from Denver to Paris.

The airline said it will also resume three-times-weekly service from San Francisco to Tel Aviv on March 28, 2027.

articles.title: US judge denies Ghislaine Maxwell’s ‘frivolous’ bid to throw out conviction
articles.summary: US judge rejects Maxwell’s claims that newly released Epstein files could help overturn her sex-trafficking convictions.
articles.body:
A United States federal judge has rejected the bid from Ghislaine Maxwell, former girlfriend and longtime associate of Jeffrey Epstein, to throw out her five felony convictions, calling the claims “meritless” and “frivolous”.

In a 67-page opinion made public on Tuesday, Judge Paul Engelmayer denied Maxwell’s post-conviction challenge to her five felony convictions.

Maxwell, 64, is serving a 20-year sentence for helping the late financier Jeffrey Epstein recruit and sexually abuse underage girls for over a decade. She is eligible for release in 2037.

She was convicted by a jury in December 2021 on five felony counts. The Second Circuit Court of Appeals upheld the verdict in 2024, and the Supreme Court declined to hear a further appeal last October.

Maxwell, representing herself, submitted her petition under Section 2255, the federal statute allowing convicted defendants to challenge their sentences. Engelmayer, who did not preside over Maxwell’s original 2021 trial, called her filing a “lengthy and rambling petition”.

Much of Maxwell’s petition leaned on records released under the Epstein Files Transparency Act (EFTA) , a law passed with near-unanimous congressional support in November 2025 that forced the US Department of Justice to make the files public.

Maxwell claims her constitutional rights at trial and sentencing were violated, and that the materials released as part of the EFTA support this claim.

Engelmayer found that the material worked against Maxwell rather than for her. “To the extent it is relevant,” he wrote, “far from exculpating her, it incriminates her or reinforces the correctness of the legal rulings Maxwell challenges.”

The judge also highlighted an apparent contradiction in Maxwell’s own account. On claims related to a sentencing enhancement, which increased her prison term because prosecutors argued she had a leadership role in Epstein’s scheme, her petition argued she had “largely exited” Epstein’s household by 2002.

But in a July 2025 interview with then-Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche, Maxwell described continuing to manage Epstein’s properties and staff years later.

On claims that Maxwell was unfairly singled out while other associates of Epstein went uncharged, Engelmayer noted she had not implicated any other person in the child sex abuse scheme and does not even concede Epstein’s culpability in her own filing.

Engelmayer described the case against her as “the epitome of a virtuous prosecution” and certified that any appeal of his ruling “would not be taken in good faith”.

articles.title: Arizona school worker allegedly accessed a security camera that was supposed to be disabled and downloaded videos of students changing; he now faces 7 voyeurism charges
articles.summary: US News: A surveillance officer working for the Tempe Union High School District has been arrested and charged with seven counts of voyeurism after allegedly u.
articles.body: A surveillance officer working for the Tempe Union High School District has been arrested and charged with seven counts of voyeurism after allegedly using school security cameras to watch and download footage of female students changing clothes. The suspect, identified in police and court records as Antony Nikai Cruz, was arrested after an internal review of the districtâs security camera system found unauthorised access to video feeds and downloads to external devices. According to a probable cause statement and reports by local news outlets AZ Family and ABC15 Arizona, the incident happened at Corona del Sol High School in Tempe, Arizona. The camera involved was monitoring a temporary changing area for female students while the schoolâs main girlsâ locker room was closed for building renovations.Internal audit leads to police investigationThe alleged misuse was discovered during routine checks of the security system rather than through a complaint from a student or parent. On 21 August, a security supervisor reviewed the systemâs activity logs and noticed unusual views of video feeds and several file exports linked to Cruzâs account. The supervisor immediately contacted the Tempe Police Department, which opened a criminal investigation. Cruz was detained on 22 August and booked into the Tempe City Jail. Investigative records cited by local news outlets say the security systemâs download history showed several video files being transferred to external storage devices, including USB drives. Digital investigators also traced cloud access to the security system to an IP address linked to Cruzâs home. During police questioning, Cruz admitted accessing the camera feeds and downloading the footage for personal use. However, he denied trying to sell, trade or share the recordings with other people. After his first court appearance, a judge set his bond at $100,000.School district responds to familiesTempe Union High School District Superintendent Stacia Wilson confirmed the charges in a message sent to parents and staff. She also addressed the police investigation taking place at the school. "As you know from my prior message, yesterday we were notified that a Tempe Union employee was detained and questioned by Tempe PD. This employee has now been booked on seven counts of voyeurism," Wilson wrote in the district message, as reported by the Arizona Daily Independent. "We know that this is a distressing situation and these details are unsettling to our families. We want to be as transparent as we are allowed to be without disrupting Tempe PD's investigation." Wilson said the district currently believes the alleged misuse was limited to one camera at Corona del Sol High School. "We are now able to share with you that the incidents leading to these charges affected Corona del Sol. As of right now, we believe that the inappropriate usage of security footage was isolated to one camera on campus," Wilson stated. "We are working closely and in full cooperation with Tempe PD as they continue to investigate and identify victims." District officials said police officers and school crisis teams would remain on campus to support students and provide counselling and other resources. Detectives are reviewing video records to identify all students who may have been filmed. "Tempe PD detectives will be on campus tomorrow to work with administration to identify the victims," Wilson added. "Once victims have been identified, Tempe PD will reach out directly to affected families to begin the interview process. Our school and District crisis teams will be in place tomorrow to provide support and resources to affected students."Charges and investigationThe Tempe Police Department said it takes the misuse of school security systems seriously and stressed the importance of protecting students and staff. âThe Tempe Police Department takes the unauthorized use of security footage seriously. Protecting the privacy and safety of students, staff and the school community remains a priority,â the department said in a statement published by YourValley.net. Under Arizona law, voyeurism is a Class 5 felony under Arizona Revised Statutes Â§ 13-3019. The law prohibits secretly viewing, filming or recording someone without consent in places where they have a reasonable expectation of privacy, including changing rooms, bathrooms and locker rooms. A Class 5 felony conviction in Arizona can carry between six months and 2.5 years in state prison for each count, along with fines of up to $150,000. The Tempe Union High School District operates six high schools serving more than 12,000 students across Maricopa County. The district said it will continue reviewing its IT systems and security camera checks as the criminal case moves through the Maricopa County court system. Police detectives are still investigating the case, including the timeline of the alleged recordings and whether additional files may exist on seized devices.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Analysis: With UNIFIL set to leave, Lebanon seeks U.N.-backed successor
articles.summary: Lebanon wants to preservie a United Nations role in the south after the current peacekeeping force leaves, Lebanese and Western analysts said.
articles.body:
BEIRUT, Lebanon, Aug. 25 (UPI) -- Lebanon, struggling to secure an Israeli withdrawal from occupied parts of southern Lebanon and restore its sovereignty, is facing another challenge: preserving a United Nations role in the south after the current peacekeeping force leaves, Lebanese and Western analysts said.

Without an U.N.-mandated international presence, Lebanon risks losing an important source of protection and leverage and could find itself increasingly at the mercy of Israel and the United States -- the two countries that have pushed hardest to terminate the U.N. peacekeeping mission.

The issue is gaining urgency, as the mandate of the U.N. Interim Force in Lebanon, or UNIFIL -- originally established after Israel's first invasion of southern Lebanon in 1978 to help confirm an Israeli withdrawal and assist the Lebanese government in re-establishing its authority -- is to expire at the end of this year.

Ironically, UNIFIL, tasked with maintaining peace in southern Lebanon for nearly five decades, is scheduled to leave as Lebanon once again negotiates -- this time through U.S.-brokered direct talks with Israel -- a new Israeli withdrawal and the future security of its southern territory.

Fearing a potential vacuum after multinational peacekeepers depart, Lebanon -- backed by a petition signed by 86 parliamentarians -- is pushing to keep UNIFIL in place, despite knowing that the effort will face opposition from Israel and the United States, while simultaneously seeking support for a replacement force under U.N. auspices.

Israel has strongly criticized UNIFIL for failing to fulfill its mission, accusing the force of allowing Hezbollah to strengthen its military presence in southern Lebanon since the 2006 war -- in violation of U.N. Security Council Resolution 1701. It is therefore unlikely to agree to any U.N. role in the future.

For the United States, terminating UNIFIL's role fits within President Donald Trump's broader efforts to sideline the U.N. and diminish its role in addressing global crises. Washington also appears to favor a new mechanism outside the existing U.N. framework.

However, blaming UNIFIL for the situation in southern Lebanon overlooks the complex realities on the ground, as well as the responsibilities of the warring parties and the international community.

Lebanese retired Maj. Gen. Abdul Rahman Chehaitli, who previously served as a liaison officer between the Lebanese government and UNIFIL, said Israel and Hezbollah have been preparing for their next confrontation since the 2006 war, rather than demobilizing or laying the groundwork for lasting peace.

While Israel was strengthening its intelligence, targeting, defensive and ground war capabilities along its northern front, Hezbollah was rebuilding and expanding its military capabilities, including weapons stockpiles, defensive positions and underground infrastructure in southern Lebanon in anticipation of another Israeli invasion.

"All the countries were seeing these preparations," Chehaitli told UPI, dismissing Gaza and Iran as "superficial pretexts" for the wars and escalations between Hezbollah and Israel in 2023 and 2026.

He noted that UNIFIL, which grew significantly in size and scope after the 2006 Israel-Hezbollah war, "did not fail in its mission, but rather carried out its duties," intervening directly on numerous occasions to prevent military escalations.

But, he said, the peacekeeping force could not stop a war once either side had made the decision to fight, adding, "It cannot prevent a war made by a decision."

Chehaitli, who was involved in post-2026 negotiations on the implementation of Resolution 1701 aimed at ending hostilities, said UNIFIL also played a role in managing border disputes between Lebanon and Israel and assisting the Lebanese Army and residents of southern Lebanon.

However, the challenges facing UNIFIL were numerous, reflecting the limitations of its mandate and the powers it was actually given.

UNIFIL spokesperson Kandice Ardiel said the role of peacekeepers has never been to enforce Resolution 1701, but to support the parties, monitor and report on its implementation.

"The main challenge has always been the incomplete commitment by Lebanon and Israel implementing their obligations under Security Council resolutions," Ardiel told UPI. "Over the years, continued violations have undermined trust and complicated efforts to achieve lasting stability."

She also cited the challenges posed by conflict, unauthorized weapons in southern Lebanon and the Israeli presence north of the Blue Line -- the U.N.-identified line of withdrawal used to confirm Israel's pullout -- as well as restrictions on peacekeepers' freedom of movement and attacks against them.

However, Ardiel emphasized UNIFIL's "important contribution" to security and stability along the Blue line for almost 17 years thanks to the peacekeepers' "visible presence," liaison and coordination role to help prevent unintended escalation during periods of tension.

"From 2006 to 2023, the Blue Line saw the longest period of relative stability in recent history, allowing a whole generation of young people to grow up there without knowing conflict," she said.

Israel's intensive military campaign has killed 8,915 people and wounded 30,543 since October 8, 2023, according to a tally released by Lebanon's Ministry of Information last Friday. It caused massive destruction to property and infrastructure, with some 70 border villages in southern Lebanon reduced to rubble and rendered uninhabitable.

An important aspect of UNIFIL's mission has been the impartial recording of what happens on the ground, including violations by the parties. Its departure, therefore, would mean losing a credible witness whose reports provide an independent record of events and violations in southern Lebanon.

As the recent war revealed the extent of Hezbollah's military presence south of the Litani River, including an extensive network of underground tunnels, questions emerged over whether -- and to what extent -- UNIFIL should be held responsible.

Ardiel said U.N. peacekeepers had, over the years, reported locations and activities of concern to the Lebanese authorities and the Security Council, noting that they "had detected and reported suspected tunnel infrastructure" before the escalation of the conflict in late 2023. However, they were not authorized to enter private property without the necessary permission.

Hezbollah, for its part, would mobilize civilian supporters to block their access, a practice that became increasingly common, according to observers.

David Wood, a senior Lebanon analyst at the International Crisis Group, emphasized that UNIFIL never had a mandate to actively enforce disarmament by confronting Hezbollah. Rather, its role was to support the Lebanese Army, which, "for its own reasons," has not sought to confront Hezbollah or force it to withdraw from the area south of the Litani River.

In fact, the Lebanese Army needed the go-ahead from the political authorities, which for years supported Hezbollah's powerful armed presence and its claim to maintain an armed resistance, according to observers.

Today, Lebanon's new leadership is keen to restore its sovereignty at a time when Hezbollah has been significantly weakened by the war, while Israel has shown little willingness to relinquish the military upper hand and gains it achieved during its campaign against the Iran-backed group.

However, ending the war and securing Israel's withdrawal from southern Lebanon would require an international force on the ground -- a replacement for UNIFIL that Lebanon is discussing with European powers.

According to Wood, by far the preferable course for any new international force would be to operate under a U.N. Security Council mandate, providing "international legitimacy and backing to protect the (participating) troops," while also securing Israeli and U.S. consent.

Chehaitli warned that any new force without international cover or authority grounded in international law would leave Lebanon "at the mercy" of the United States and Israel, which "is now treating Lebanon as a weak country and imposing its conditions on it."

"UNIFIL used to put Lebanon at the same level of Israel, not as Lebanon is weak and Israel is strong, and used to be not only a witness but also a referee," he said.

He expressed concern that a new force without a U.N. mandate could face conflicts of interest among its participating countries and risk pushing Lebanon to the margins of international attention.

articles.title: U.K. estate used as Wayne Manor in "Batman Begins" must be surveyed for bats
articles.summary: Since being built in the 1850s, Mentmore Towers has been featured in "Batman Begins" and other movies, but has fallen into disrepair.
articles.body:
A British estate used as a filming location in Christopher Nolan's "Batman Begins" may be taken from its owners if repair work, including bat surveys, does not commence, according to local council notices.

The stately home was built between 1852 and 1854 in Buckinghamshire, a region in southeast England. It stood in for Wayne Manor in the 2005 superhero blockbuster, which starred Christian Bale and Katie Holmes .

Buckinghamshire Council served the company that owns the estate with a formal listed-buildings repair notice amid reports of deteriorating conditions at the property. CBS News partner BBC News reported that the notice was dated Aug. 4.

The building could be placed on the market – unless the owners show evidence that a licensed bat ecologist has been appointed to conduct surveys. The owners have one month to begin the process and provide evidence, council deputy leader Peter Strachan told CBS News. If the notice is not dealt with, the council could seek government approval to acquire the mansion, though this would be subject to further legal action, according to the BBC.

Mentmore Towers is considered a Grade I heritage building, which means it must have a special architectural or historical interest. Around 2.5% of buildings in the United Kingdom, including Buckingham Palace and the Tower of London, are among the Grade I-listed buildings that have been preserved.

The property has been owned by Mentmore Towers Limited since 1999. That company is owned by Simon Halabi, a Syrian-British property developer. In 2007, Halabi was named Britain's 14th richest man, according to The Times . However, in 2010, the tycoon was declared bankrupt over a $76 million loan he received from a failed Icelandic bank .

In addition to being used in "Batman Begins," Mentmore Towers was also featured in other films, including "The Mummy Returns" and "Johnny English." It was also used as a filming location in the Spice Girls' music video for the 1998 song "Goodbye." Before appearing onscreen, it was home to the Rothschild family. But despite its famous past, the building has "fallen into an increasingly worsening state of disrepair over recent years," the council told CBS News.

Historic England, a public body responsible for advising the government on protecting historic sites, lists the building as being in "very bad" condition and at risk of "further rapid deterioration." The organization noted that Mentmore Towers is on its Heritage at Risk register, "which identifies sites most at risk of being lost through neglect, decay or inappropriate development."

The BBC describes the building as having deteriorating roofs, chimneys, rooflights, roof lanterns and leadwork. According to Save Britain's Heritage , an independent charity that works to protect and restore historic buildings in England, permissions to repair the roof were granted in 2016, but the work was not completed.

The ecological survey is the first step of the repair work. By August 2027, the property owners must have conducted three such surveys, as well as acquired any essential historical licenses to undertake the necessary repairs.

The BBC reported that the owners must demonstrate that they are taking steps to appoint a contractor with appropriate experience for repairing listed buildings and roofs that are of similar size and historic appearance. Once repair work begins, Buckinghamshire Council and Historic England officers must be allowed to inspect it weekly, the BBC reported.

"We welcome this action taken by Buckinghamshire Council requiring the current owner to carry out urgent and overdue repairs to this great house," said Henrietta Billings, the director of Save Britain's Heritage. "We urge the owners, who have owned the building for over 25 years, to step up and undertake immediate repairs. This exceptional landmark has been neglected for too long."

articles.title: Germany's Merz warns attackers will 'pay price' after drone incident
articles.summary: A drone attack on Leipzig Airport highlights the "very real threat" faced by the country, the German chancellor says.
articles.body:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has warned that those responsible for drone attacks and other hostile acts against Germany, including a recent case at Leipzig Airport, would "pay a price".

Merz said the incident showed Germany was "facing a very real threat" and was increasingly becoming a target.

On 4 August, a drone carrying an explosive device was discovered at Leipzig/Halle Airport in eastern Germany, close to Ukrainian cargo planes. However, it failed to explode as the detonator was apparently faulty.

Police defused the explosives and believe a second drone may have collided with a cargo aircraft nearby. Security experts have speculated that Russia may have been responsible.

The German government has made no direct accusations. Moscow has denied involvement.

Leipzig/Halle Airport is used by the Germany military and Nato allies for the transport of military goods and also serves as a base for Ukraine's Antonov Airlines - which carry most of the country's aerial cargo. It is also a major hub for logistics group DHL.

"We have problems, some of which stem from outside the country, and which we must not ignore," Merz said.

"Attackers are increasingly ruthless, accepting even severe property damage, and even injuries and fatalities."

According to German reports, investigators have since found a third drone near Leipzig airport.

Public broadcasters NDR, WDR and the SÃ¼ddeutsche Zeitung newspaper also reported that traces of the military explosive hexogen were found nearby.

Speaking on the margins of a government coalition retreat at Neuhardenberg, Merz said the government was working closely with the security authorities on the case and would release more details soon.

Merz also vowed to "stay the course" supporting Ukraine in its fight against Russia's invasion.

"The government is continuing its support for Ukraine with steadfast resolve," he said. "Today, we are its strongest supporter - not to prolong the war, but to force peace talks."

Germany, he said, was initiating a range of measures to better protect itself against such attacks.

These include stronger drone defences and plans to empower security services to strike back against attackers at home and abroad, for example by hacking their computer servers.

There has been a series of unauthorised drone flights in recent months over sensitive sites in Germany including military bases, airports, energy terminals, seaports and logistics companies.

Police have warned that the overflights could have been organised by Russian agents.

articles.title: Gun-running ship located 78 years after being sunk by Israeli military
articles.summary: In June 1948, Israeli forces opened fire and sank the boat in waters off Tel Aviv on the orders of David Ben Gurion, Israel's first prime minister.
articles.body:
Israel announced on Monday it had recovered the wreckage of the Altalena, an arms-smuggling boat whose sinking by the Israeli military just after the state's founding in 1948 exposed divisions that persist today.

The Altalena had set sail from France loaded with weapons packed for the Irgun, the militant Zionist force that conducted attacks against the British colonial authorities and the local Palestinian population in the quest to establish Israel.

In June 1948, Israeli forces opened fire and sank the boat in waters off Tel Aviv on the orders of David Ben Gurion, Israel's first prime minister. He wanted to exert his authority and prevent the emergence of any paramilitary rival to the Israeli military in the month-old state, which was in the throes of war with neighboring Arab countries.

"At 12:30 am, at a depth of 503 meters, west of the coast of Israel, the Altalena ship was located intact — 78 years after that painful and seminal event that shook the young State of Israel," Heritage Minister Amihai Eliyahu said.

Sixteen Irgun members and three Israeli soldiers were killed. Irgun chief Menachem Begin asked his fighters to surrender to Israeli authorities with words that would become famous: "There will be no civil war with the enemy at our gates."

After the violence, the burned-out vessel remained off the Tel Aviv coast before eventually being towed out to sea and sunk, according to the Jerusalem Post , which published a computer image of the remains of the ship on the seafloor.

The conflict pitted against each other the two political blocs that would define Israel. Begin became prime minister in 1977, ushering in the rise of right-wing nationalists and sweeping out the socialist movement launched under Ben Gurion.

Eliyahu, who announced the salvaging of the Altalena, hails from the far-right, which has taken power as part of a government led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

He called the Altalena "the story of a deep national wound, and the story of the historical responsibility that Menachem Begin showed when he prevented a civil war."

"A country that is not afraid to touch on the painful chapters of its history is a stronger country," he said.

Israel erected a monument to the fallen Altalena militants in 2008 on the Tel Aviv seafront and has been searching for the wreckage for years, with crews often working in secrecy.

It was not immediately known what would happen to the ship's wreckage.

"Finding Altalena is not an opportunity to renew old disputes," the Ben Gurion Heritage Institute wrote on social media after the ship's discovery. "It is an opportunity to remind why statism is not a slogan — but a condition for the existence of a state."

articles.title: Georgia sheriffâs office arrested a second deputy in one month over alleged Flock misuse; latest case involved someone he had a personal relationship with
articles.summary: US News: A second Habersham County Sheriff's Office deputy has been fired and arrested in less than a month after an internal audit found he allegedly used the.
articles.body: A second Habersham County Sheriff's Office deputy has been fired and arrested in less than a month after an internal audit found he allegedly used the department's automated license plate reader system to track someone with whom he had a personal relationship. Former deputy Jonathan Thomas, who joined the department on 2 December 2024, was arrested during an ongoing review of how officers use surveillance technology. Thomas has been charged with felony violation of oath of office and a misdemeanor count of misusing license plate data, according to a statement from the Habersham County Sheriff's Office reported by 11Alive. He was later booked into the Habersham County Detention Center. Thomas's dismissal is the second case in several weeks involving alleged misuse of the agency's Flock Safety system. It follows the late July arrest of former deputy Christian Brewer, who faced the same charges after allegedly using the database to track someone he knew personally.Internal review finds second caseThe latest case was uncovered during a wider review by department leaders to make sure access to the database was being used only for legitimate law enforcement investigations. "As we continue to conduct our audit into the use of our Flock system, we have discovered a second deputy who accessed Flock outside of its intended law enforcement purpose," said Habersham County Sheriff Robin Krockum in a public statement reported by 11Alive. The July arrest of Brewer, who had worked for the sheriff's office since May 2024, led command staff to expand their checks of the system. In that case, WSB-TV Channel 2 reported that Krockum personally addressed the misuse and stressed the importance of public trust. "The people of Habersham County trust us with authority and access to sensitive information," Krockum said in a statement published by WSB-TV. "This trust is earned every day and can be lost in a single decision. Any misuse of our authority or the tools provided to your deputies is a betrayal of that trust. Although this was an isolated incident, I will not tolerate misconduct. We will hold our own accountable because the public we serve deserves no less."New rules for surveillance accessFollowing the two cases, the Habersham County Sheriff's Office has introduced tighter rules for accessing license plate data. According to WSB-TV Channel 2 and All On Georgia, the agency reduced the number of employees allowed to conduct certain license plate searches from 39 to 23 designated supervisory officers. Under the new rules, deputies can no longer search the regional database on their own. Every search must first be approved by a supervisor. The supervisor must record the reason for the search and enter a valid, active criminal case number into the system. Deputies must also contact the county dispatch centre by radio so that every search is recorded in the official log. "We will continue to audit our system and hold those accountable who have abused this system," Krockum said in a statement published by 11Alive. "We will continue to be transparent to the public in the way we conduct ourselves and hold those responsible who violate their trust." Flock Safety technology uses networks of fixed cameras to photograph passing vehicles. The cameras record licence plates, vehicle make, model, colour and other identifying features, along with the time and location of each image. The system does not directly show vehicle ownership or personal driver records. However, it stores location data for 30 days, allowing authorised users to see where a particular vehicle has travelled across participating areas.Georgia faces wider scrutinyThe two Habersham County arrests are part of a wider focus on the use of automated camera systems by law enforcement agencies across Georgia. Reports from Hoodline and Now Georgia say internal audits and investigations by the Georgia Bureau of Investigation have led to criminal charges or resignations involving more than 20 law enforcement employees across the state over unauthorised searches of surveillance data. Recent cases include four former Savannah Police Department employees who were arrested following an internal review. Three former Bibb County Sheriff's Office deputies were also charged with stalking and unlawfully keeping license plate information after allegedly accessing records involving personal acquaintances. Similar investigations into camera and license plate data have taken place in Cherokee, DeKalb, Coweta, Greene and Albany counties. The felony charges against the former Habersham County deputies fall under Georgia Code Â§ 16-10-1, which covers violation of oath by a public officer. A conviction can carry a prison sentence of one to five years. The related misdemeanor charge falls under Georgia Code Â§ 35-1-22, which sets rules for the use of automated license plate reader data and prohibits searches that are not for official purposes. The Habersham County Sheriff's Office said the criminal investigation into Thomas remains active. Once the investigation is complete, the final case file will be sent to the District Attorney's Office for further legal proceedings.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Colombia orders raids targeting migrants without legal status
articles.summary: Colombian President Abelardo De la Espriella ordered police and immigration authorities to begin to identify and deport migrants without legal status.
articles.body:
Aug. 25 (UPI) -- Colombian President Abelardo De la Espriella ordered police and immigration authorities to begin to identify and deport migrants without legal status, starting in Barranquilla, the president's office said.

De la Espriella issued the order during a security council meeting in the Caribbean city, where he announced measures to combat homicide, extortion, drug trafficking and other crimes, according to an official statement .

"The order to Migration is clear: coordinated operations with the police must begin in Barranquilla to find illegal immigrants," De la Espriella said.

The president said authorities would first target foreign nationals committing crimes and then those who have not regularized their immigration status in Colombia.

"This is a presidential order that must begin to be carried out this week," he said. "I will not accept illegal immigrants, regardless of where they come from, who are committing crimes in Colombia. They will leave, and we will deport them."

De la Espriella said the measure was a political and administrative decision by his government. However, the announcement did not include a decree, an enforcement protocol or a deportation target.

The government also has not explained whether the order changes existing legal standards or seeks to intensify enforcement already carried out by Colombia's immigration authority.

Deportations and expulsions were already part of Colombia's immigration policy. Between August 2022 and June, Migration Colombia documented 3,389 deportations and 2,576 expulsions -- a total of 5,965 people.

The leading reasons for deportation during that period were remaining in the country without legal status, with 1,380 cases, and entering or leaving the country illegally, with 1,315, according to Migration Colombia .

Other cases involved fraudulent documents, false statements, unauthorized activities, court orders and threats to national security or public order. The immigration authority said deportations and expulsions require individual administrative proceedings.

The decision fulfills a campaign promise. In June, when he was still a candidate, De la Espriella said foreign nationals who entered Colombia legally would receive guarantees, while those who violated immigration rules would be returned to their home countries, El Colombiano reported.

Colombia is home to more than 2.8 million Venezuelans, the country's largest foreign population. Migration Colombia had registered 2,831,561 Venezuelan nationals intending to settle in Colombia as of Aug. 31, 2025, according to an official report .

The Association of Venezuelans in Barranquilla called on authorities to respect due process and the right to a defense during the new operations.

"Anyone who commits a crime must answer to the justice system, regardless of whether they are Colombian, Venezuelan or any other nationality," the organization said. However, it warned that "irregular immigration status is not synonymous with criminality," according to Caracol Radio.

articles.title: Monaghan: Man charged with possession of Semtex near Irish border granted bail
articles.summary: Simon O'Donovan, 44, of Sperrin Road in Dublin 12 was granted bail during a hearing at the High Court.
articles.body:
A Dublin museum employee charged over the seizure of a Semtex explosive device which was described as capable of causing "catastrophic damage and serious loss of life", has been granted €40,000 (£34,000) bail.

Simon O'Donovan, 44, of Sperrin Road in Dublin 12 was previously remanded in custody.

However, on Tuesday he was granted bail during a hearing at the High Court, which heard that he was a member of the dissident-aligned republican group Saoradh.

A Garda (Irish police) Special Detective Unit (SDU) officer objected to bail, voicing concerns that O'Donovan "would continue to engage in operational activities to further the aims of New IRA".

He was arrested following an SDU operation which led to a car being stopped in County Monaghan near the border in July.

O'Donovan is charged with possessing an explosive improvised device on 22 July at St Laurence's Road, Chapelizod, Dublin 10.

Mr Justice Mícheál P. O'Higgins noted that gardaí objected to bail, but granted it subject to strict conditions.

O'Donovan must lodge €10,000 (£8,500) personally and needs approval from an independent surety with €30,000 (£25,600) available, which will be frozen in their account.

The surety has yet to be confirmed and can be endorsed later in the District Court.

He has surrendered his passport and must stay at his current address, obey a 22:00 – 07:00 local time curfew, provide a contact mobile phone number on which he is available 24/7, sign-on daily at a local garda station, have no direct or indirect contact with members of the political group Saoradh, or engage in any of that movement's events.

The terms state that he must stay out of the Dublin 7 area and the Collins Barrack National Museum in the capital, and have no contact with witnesses or law student Isobella Perrie Sullivan, who is a co-accused in the case.

SDU Det Sgt Shane Noone said he remained concerned that O'Donovan would commit other offences and also interfere with witnesses in the case.

He alleged that the accused, who appeared via video link, was "captured on CCTV at 13.33 on 22 July, leaving his place of employment, Collins Barracks Museum, with a distinctive holdall bag in his possession".

The bail hearing was told O'Donovan worked at the museum for a decade and held a position of deputy facilities officer.

The det sgt maintained that the accused was "tracked" on CCTV cycling to the War Memorial Gardens and meeting his co-accused 20 minutes later.

It was alleged he was observed at St Lawrence Road showing Perrie Sullivan the contents of the bag, which she took before driving by car to Aclint south of Carrickmacross in County Monaghan, where she was stopped by members attached to the SDU.

Noone maintained that the bag that had previously been in O'Donovan's possession was in the back of the vehicle.

The court heard gardaí recovered 394 grams of military-grade Semtex, a timer, a timing switch and a viable detonator.

Noone said that on arrest the accused replied: "This is harassment because I am a member of Saoradh", which the SDU officer described as a far-left political group formed by dissident republicans in the Republic and Northern Ireland.

He added it was formed in 2016 and aligned with the New IRA.

It was accepted the accused had no warrant history for failing to appear in court.

He told the court that the device was transported to and stored at the museum, which "posed a risk to members of the public and tourists, not to mention targets".

The det sgt said O'Donovan showed "blatant disregard".

"An unintended detonation would have caused catastrophic damage and serious loss of life or serious injury," he said.

The court heard it has been confirmed that there was Semtex in the bag seized at Aclint.

Voicing concerns about witness interference, Noone said the SDU has conducted a significant investigation to date, involving numerous avenues and witnesses.

It was put to the officer by O'Donovan's barrister, that he made much of the fact that the accused was a member of a political party, suggesting he would intimidate witnesses, while omitting the detail that he denied the offence after being brought to a garda station.

The det sgt replied that his political association remained relevant.

Counsel also outlined that he was an only son, and the primary carer for elderly sick parents.

Noone conceded he had no concerns regarding a flight risk, and it was accepted that the accused is in a long-term relationship.

O'Donovan will remain in custody with consent to bail until all funds have been provided as stipulated.

He is due back before the non-jury Special Criminal Court on 5 October.

articles.title: Most US Democrats in early 2028 primary states oppose aid to Israel: Poll
articles.summary: Survey indicates majority of Democrats in first six states to vote for 2028 nominee believe Israel committing genocide.
articles.body:
Most United States Democratic voters in states that will play a key role in choosing the party’s nominee in the 2028 presidential election oppose providing aid and weapons to Israel, a new poll suggests.

The survey, released late on Monday by the IMEU Policy Project, a think tank that supports Palestinians’ human rights, is the latest indication of Israel’s dwindling popularity in the US, especially among Democrats.

Conducted by the research firm YouGov, the poll found that the majority of voters in South Carolina, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan and Virginia believe Israel is committing genocide in Gaza .

These states will hold the first primary contests in the 2028 elections and play an outsized role in choosing the Democratic nominee and possibly the next US president.

In Michigan, 80 percent of respondents, including 91 percent of voters under the age of 45, answered “yes” to the question “Do you believe Israel is committing genocide against Palestinians living in Gaza?”

A majority of 52 percent of respondents in South Carolina, which will hold the first Democratic primary of the 2028 campaign, said they oppose selling arms to Israel, which would amount to an arms embargo on the US ally if put into practice.

Respondents across all six states also showed support for imposing sanctions on Israel and enforcing the International Criminal Court’s arrest warrant against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu .

Hamid Bendaas, a spokesperson for IMEU Policy Project, said a key takeaway from the survey is that support for Israel in the Democratic base has become negligible.

For example, in South Carolina, only 2 percent of respondents said they favour military support for Israel.

Bendaas also noted that voters back strong policies against Israel, such as sanctions, that are seen as unrealistic by the mainstream media.

“These things when they’re discussed, it’s often as ‘This is something that is out of the mainstream’, but they’re overwhelmingly supported by the voters who are probably going to be pretty decisive in deciding the next nominee for president in the Democratic Party,” Bendaas told Al Jazeera.

The Democratic Party finalised its 2028 primary calendar this month and made South Carolina the site of its first nomination contest on January 22, followed by weekly elections in the five remaining states.

These first primaries will likely give enormous momentum to the top finishers and weed out contenders who fail to make a mark early on.

The vote is still 16 months away, but the IMEU findings, which match the data of other polls, could play a role in shaping the platforms of Democratic candidates on the issue.

Israel has been rapidly losing support among Democrats for years, a trend that was accelerated by its genocidal war on Gaza , which began in October 2023.

But the Democratic leadership has maintained its backing of Israel. The US, under former Democratic President Joe Biden, who described himself as a Zionist, provided Israel with tens of billions of dollars as it turned nearly all of Gaza into rubble.

Current Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries , the top Democrat in the House of Representatives, are also staunch supporters of Israel.

Still, cracks in the decades-long bipartisan support for Israel in Washington have been widening in recent years. In July, more than 100 Democrats in the House – nearly half of the party’s caucus – voted to block weapons to Israel.

And with progressive critics of Israel winning Democratic congressional primaries across the map , policy on Israel-Palestine is likely to play a key role in the presidential primaries in 2028.

This month, Abdul El-Sayed stunned the Democratic establishment when he overcame more than $60m in campaign spending by his pro-Israel opponent to win the party’s nomination for a US Senate seat in Michigan.

Bendaas said the 2028 presidential race could further close the gap between public opinion and the Democratic Party’s policies, arguing that any candidate vying for the presidential nomination would need to align with voters on the issue.

“When that happens, when you have a new leader who takes a new position, that really does help parties shift more rapidly,” he told Al Jazeera. “Unfortunately, the current leadership as it stands in the Democratic Party has been people who have a very status quo view about the US-Israel relationship. And so, what ultimately needs to happen is the party just needs a new leader who actually reflects its voters.”

articles.title: West Bank settlers attack AFP journalists
articles.summary: Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank on Tuesday attacked AFP journalists reporting on tension with Palestinians, in violence that left at least five pe...
articles.body:
Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank on Tuesday attacked AFP journalists reporting on tension with Palestinians, in violence that left at least five people injured, the reporters and medics said.

A three-person team from the international news agency had travelled to the village of Jannatah near Bethlehem to report on Israeli activists who conduct solidarity visits to support Palestinians facing harassment by Israeli settlers, who recently blocked a road in the area.

After an altercation broke out between the settlers and activists, the Israeli military ordered journalists to leave what it called a "closed military zone", at which point two additional cars full of settlers swooped in.

The settlers, many of them children, threw stones towards the journalists and activists. One AFP journalist ducked a stone but then a child settler struck him in the chin with a stick, causing minor bleeding, he said.

The AFP journalists returned to see their two parked cars both damaged, with back windshields smashed in and tyres punctured. Activists' cars suffered similar damage.

Five people were treated for injuries, the Palestine Red Crescent Society said, with AFP journalists reporting seeing at least one Israeli activist taken in a Palestinian ambulance.

During the clash an Israeli soldier temporarily seized the camera of a video journalist but handed it back afterward, the AFP journalists said.

An Israeli military spokesperson said that the temporary confiscation of the camera "is currently being reviewed".

Israeli police joined the military to collect evidence on the damage to cars and "a police investigation has been opened into the incident", the military spokesperson said.

More than 500,000 Israelis live in the West Bank, which Israel has occupied since 1967, home to around three million Palestinians, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing government advancing more construction ahead of October 27 elections.

Violence against Palestinians by Israeli settlers has increased dramatically since the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel by Hamas from the Gaza Strip.

articles.title: Map shows countries paying people to have babies as birth rate drops
articles.summary: In one country, children can receive up to $55,000 by the time they turn 17.
articles.body:
Governments around the world are increasingly offering cash payments, tax breaks, housing subsidies and childcare support in an effort to persuade citizens to have more children as birth rates fall and populations age.

Declining birth rates can strain a country's economy because there aren't enough people being born to support the aging population. That means greater strains on social programs like Social Security and Medicare in the United States since more and more people are using the programs, but not enough people are paying into them. Declining birth rates are a global problem, and a growing number of countries are rolling out increasingly generous pro-family incentives, ranging from direct payments for newborns to years of childcare assistance.

Singapore has spent years expanding financial support for families as it grapples with one of the world's lowest fertility rates. Prime Minister Lawrence Wong recently announced a major expansion of family support measures, emphasizing that the government wants to provide assistance well beyond a child's birth and into the early years of parenting.

Each child will receive almost S$70,000, the equivalent of about $55,000 USD, in direct financial support by the time they turn 17. The program will replace the current program, which includes the Baby Bonus Scheme.

Under the Baby Bonus Scheme, parents are given cash gifts throughout the first six-and-a-half years of a child's life. The first and second child get a total of S$11,000, equivalent to about $8,660 USD, disbursed in six-month increments, and every other child gets S$13,000, equivalent to about $10,236 USD.

Under the Large Families Scheme, which will also be replaced when the new package goes into effect, families can receive an additional $16,000 for each third or subsequent child born after February 18, 2025.

Despite those efforts, Singapore's birth rate remains among the lowest globally. The cash incentives began in 2001 and haven't been able to reverse the declining trend in birth rates.

"Ultimately, the decision to have children is a deeply personal one. Policies alone cannot make this happen. But what we can do is make it easier for Singaporeans who want children to start and raise a family," Wong said in a statement.

China has dramatically shifted from restricting births to actively encouraging them.

After decades of the one-child policy, Chinese officials are now trying to boost fertility as births have fallen and the population has begun shrinking. In 2025, Beijing rolled out a nationwide childcare subsidy that provides families with 3,600 yuan, or about $500, annually for each child under age three.

The subsidy is part of a broader campaign to encourage childbirth and ease the cost of raising children. Chinese authorities have also supported local initiatives that offer even larger payments, including monthly stipends and bonuses for families with multiple children.

"International practices show that cash subsidies are an indispensable part of pro-birth measures," Zhang Benbo, a researcher at a think tank under the National Development and Reform Commission, said in a statement at the time.

The national program is expected to benefit millions of households each year and reflects mounting concern over China's aging population and shrinking workforce.

Japan has become one of the world's most prominent examples of a nation battling demographic decline.

The country's aging population and persistently low fertility rate have prompted officials to expand financial support for families. Government measures include monthly child allowances, a childbirth lump-sum grant that has been increased to 500,000 yen, equivalent to $3,139 USD, and expanded childcare services.

Japan is also launching new childcare and education support initiatives in 2026. These reforms aim to reduce the financial burden of raising children by expanding access to childcare regardless of employment status and broadening financial assistance for families. While unveiling a policy to promote people having kids in 2023, Children's Policies Minister Masanobu Ogura said the next few years are possibly "a last chance" for Japan to change the trajectory of its declining birth rate.

"While diverse views about marriage, childbirth and childrearing should be respected, we want to make a society where young generations can marry, have and raise children as they wish," Ogura said, according to the Associated Press. "The basic direction of our measures to tackle low births is to reverse the trend of declining births by supporting individuals' pursuit of happiness."

Officials have repeatedly said the country's future economic strength depends in part on stabilizing population trends.

South Korea has spent billions of dollars attempting to increase what has frequently been ranked as the world's lowest fertility rate. The government offers an extensive package of benefits that includes monthly allowances for parents, direct birth grants, childcare support, expanded parental leave and housing assistance.

South Korea launched a program in 2022 that gave mothers 2 million won, the equivalent of about $1,500 USD, when they gave birth and then an additional 700,000 won, equivalent to about $500 USD, each month until their child turns one. Then, parents get 350,000 won, equivalent to about $260 USD, per month until they turn 2.

A major South Korean company is also offering its employees incentives to have kids. The Lotte Group, a massive conglomerate, gives employees with three or more children a free 7-9 seat family vehicle, and housing group Booyoung offers employees a $75,000 bonus for each new child they have.

"Korea will face a crisis of national existence 20 years from now, including a decline in the economically productive population and a shortage of defense personnel to ensure national security and maintain order," Booyoung chairman Lee Joong Keun told CBS News in 2024.

South Korea is still struggling with its birth rate, but the number of babies born in South Korea increased in 2024, the first time in nine years.

Sweden doesn't pay a cash bonus for having kids, but provides parents with a monthly allowance depending on the number of children they have. Each eligible child is given 1,250 SEK, the equivalent of $132 USD, and families with two or more children are eligible for the Large Family Supplement.

Parents with two kids receive an additional 150 SEK per month, equivalent to $15 USD; three-child families get 730 SEK, equivalent to $77 USD; four-child households get 1,740 SEK per month, equivalent to $183 USD, and families with five or more children get an extra 1,250 SEK per month per child, equivalent to about $132 USD.

The country offers generous paid parental leave, subsidized childcare and income support designed to make balancing careers and family life easier.

Estonia has combined direct payments with broader family support programs aimed at encouraging larger families.

Parents receive childbirth allowances and other child-related benefits, with support increasing for households with multiple children. The country also offers paid parental leave and childcare policies that policymakers say help reduce the cost of raising children.

Families with one or two eligible children receive 80 euros per child per month, equivalent to $93 USD, and families with three or more eligible children receive 100 euros per child per month, equivalent to $116 USD. The payments are made to parents until children turn 19.

Estonia's family policy has long been cited internationally as an example of how financial assistance can be paired with social programs to support parents. Government officials have repeatedly emphasized that encouraging family formation requires both direct financial support and practical assistance.

Estonia's birth rate has been on the decline since 2021. The child allowance started in 1992.

Finland has adopted a combination of cash benefits and family support services to encourage child-rearing. One of the country's most famous family programs is the baby box, which provides new parents with essential supplies for newborns. Families can also receive financial assistance and monthly benefits.

Parents of eligible children receive monthly payments until the child turns 17. Families with one child receive 94.88 euros, equivalent to $110 USD, 104.84 euros for the second child, 133.79 euros for the third child, equivalent to $156.11 USD, 173.24 euros for the fourth child, equivalent to $202.15 USD, 192.69 Euros for the fifth child, equivalent to $224.84 USD.

Despite being family-friendly, Finland has one of the lowest birth rates among the Nordic countries.

"So we cannot really any longer say that it's our good family policies that explain good fertility in the Nordics," Anneli Miettinen, a research manager at Kela, told NPR in 2025.

The United Arab Emirates offers some of the most generous childbirth-related financial support programs available to citizens.

Emirati families can qualify for substantial financial assistance tied to childbirth, while lower-income households may also receive monthly child allowances. Additional benefits are available for larger families, including support related to housing and debt relief.

Depending on where a person lives, a UAE native citizen can receive up to AED 220,000, equivalent to about $60,000 USD, after the birth of their child.

One of the country's notable programs includes the NAFIS child allowance initiative, which provides monthly payments for eligible children. These policies are designed to reduce family expenses and encourage population growth among Emirati citizens. Families can get AED 600 per qualifying child each month, equivalent to $163 USD.

The benefits generally apply only to UAE nationals rather than expatriate residents, reflecting the government's focus on supporting citizen families.

Can Cash Incentives Reverse Falling Birth Rates?

While governments continue expanding family benefits, researchers remain divided on how much direct financial incentives can raise birth rates.

Studies have found that generous payments and childcare support can influence family planning decisions, particularly when combined with broader policies that reduce the long-term cost of raising children. Data show that it can cause an immediate bump, but often doesn't fix long-term population declines. As fertility rates remain below replacement levels across much of the developed world, policymakers are increasingly experimenting with new approaches.

articles.title: Jimmy Donaldson started YouTube at 13; years later the channel became the foundation of a $5 billion global business
articles.summary: US Streamers News: At just 13, Jimmy Donaldson was already uploading videos under the name âMrBeast6000â from Eastern North Carolina. What started with low-view uploads .
articles.body: At just 13, Jimmy Donaldson was already uploading videos under the name âMrBeast6000â from Eastern North Carolina. What started with low-view uploads while he was still dealing with school eventually became something much bigger than a YouTube channel. Donaldson spent years studying what made videos work, and that obsession became the base for a business empire now known as Beast Industries. The strange part is how long the early grind lasted. From 2012 to 2016, he uploaded hundreds of videos without huge numbers. During his late teens, he also spent hours on Skype with a small group of other creators. They would break down YouTube recommendations, test thumbnail layouts, compare titles and study how long viewers stayed on videos. Basically, the platform itself became their experiment.The system Jimmy Donaldson built before the big breakthroughThe big shift came in January 2017, when Donaldson posted a video of himself counting to 100,000. It took around 40 hours to complete, but the stunt helped turn him into a much bigger name.His approach to money was also pretty different. Instead of simply keeping early advertising income, Donaldson pushed it straight back into new videos. The system was simple: if one video made $10,000, he would spend $10,000 on the next one.That reinvestment kept raising the scale. Small cash giveaways eventually became elaborate sets, real islands and huge survival-style productions. Each project was built to become bigger than the previous one.From YouTube creator to Beast IndustriesVideo alone was never the final destination. Donaldson moved into consumer products, with Feastables becoming a major part of the operation. The snack brand went on to generate hundreds of millions of dollars in retail sales around the world.Beast Industries also moved into areas far outside traditional creator businesses. The company acquired teen-focused fintech platform Step and launched Beast Mobile, pushing the operation into finance and telecom.By this point, the YouTube channel was feeding a much larger corporate structure. Beast Industries, led by CEO Jeffrey Housenbold, is valued at roughly $5.2 billion, according to the information provided.MrBeastâs biggest milestones are now happening at massive scaleDonaldson later pushed the brand into television-style entertainment through Beast Games, a reality competition series made with Amazon Prime Video and backed by a huge production budget.The scale of the original channel also kept climbing. MrBeast overtook T-Series in June 2024 and then reached another major milestone on June 12, 2026, becoming the first YouTube channel to pass 500 million subscribers.His estimated net worth is around $2.6 billion, with much of that value tied to private-company equity. TIME also placed the operation on its TIME100 Most Influential Companies list. The story has moved far beyond a teenager uploading from North Carolina. What began as a channel became the engine for a diversified consumer business.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
